item.title: WaPo’s Axed Protest Reporter Leads Fired Journalists in Protest Outside Paper’s Headquarters
item.description: Fired Washington Post journalists protested outside the paper’s headquarters this week after management cut roughly 30 percent of its newsroom. They were led by Marissa J. Lang, whom the Post hired in 2018 to head the paper’s protest coverage. The post WaPo’s Axed Protest Reporter Leads Fired Journalists in Protest Outside Paper’s Headquarters appeared first on .

item.title: Columbia Professors Arrested For Blocking Traffic to Protest ICE
item.description: Two Columbia University professors were arrested for blocking traffic for nearly an hour during an anti-ICE protest outside the Ivy League school's main gates on Thursday. One was a guard for the illegal anti-Israel encampment in April 2024. The post Columbia Professors Arrested For Blocking Traffic to Protest ICE appeared first on .

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Free Beacon Debuts LeMay Awards to Keep Pace With New York Times
item.description: The New York Times seems especially pleased with itself these days. In a brazen display of self-regard, the paper has reportedly started yet another awards program for its own employees. Earlier this week, the Times announced the finalists for the "inaugural Ochs awards," named for the paper's original owner, Adolph Ochs. item.title: America Needs a New START? Our Enemies Never Stopped.
item.description: To the shock, horror, and dismay of onlookers around the world, the New START treaty expired on Thursday. item.title: Do the Ends No Longer Justify the Means?
item.description: At age 93, the magisterial Harvey Mansfield of Harvard has given us a splendid new book, The Rise and Fall of Rational Control. The title will be perplexing to most people. "What is ‘rational control’?" they will ask. And "how can such a thing, whatever it is, ‘rise and fall’?" Professor Mansfield provides a hint in the work’s subtitle: "The History of Modern Political Philosophy." The post Do the Ends No Longer Justify the Means? appeared first on .

item.title: Harry Reid and the Art of Ruthlessness
item.description: Power, not anchored to any larger principles, is a recipe for self-preservation over good governance. That's the picture that veteran Nevada political journalist Jon Ralston paints of the late former Senate majority leader Harry Reid and his worldview, in a meticulously reported if largely solicitous book about Reid's political life, The Game Changer. The post Harry Reid and the Art of Ruthlessness appeared first on .
